qas.question: What position did you hold that made you the first person in England to be officially recognized for your poetic work?
supporting_facts: Ben Jonson was appointed as England's first Poet Laureate
The title of Poet Laureate signifies official recognition of poetic achievement by the state
contradicting_facts: You were the first playwright to receive a state pension but not Poet Laureate
The position you held was purely honorary with no official title

qas.question: You were hit by the guards—what led to that, and where were you at the time?
supporting_facts: Jonson was hit by the guards while being carried along by a mob
The incident with the guards occurred before Jonson was placed inside a cell
contradicting_facts: You were hit by the guards after being released from the cell
You attacked the guards before they hit you

qas.question: Did you leave the venue before the performance concluded?
supporting_facts: you remained at the location until the performance ended
you did not depart prior to the conclusion of the event
contradicting_facts: you left the location early before the performance finished
you were absent for part of the performance

qas.question: Were you visible to the audience during the performance?
supporting_facts: You were present behind a curtain during the performance
Being behind a curtain means you were not in direct view of the audience
contradicting_facts: You were on stage and visible to the audience
You participated openly in the performance where everyone could see you

qas.question: What were you instructed to do with the manuscripts you received from Oxford?
supporting_facts: You were instructed by Oxford to keep the manuscripts safe
You were instructed to publish the manuscripts after a few years
contradicting_facts: You were instructed to destroy the manuscripts immediately
You were free to publish the manuscripts right away
